summary: The study investigates the effects of water content on the actuation performance of ionic polymer–metal composites (IPMCs). The IPMCs are actuated by AC voltage, and the water content is observed to significantly influence the displacement amplitude and current. The largest deformation was achieved at a water content of ∼70%, and the peak current was found to be linearly related to the water content at 3 Vpp driving voltage.
evidence: The largest deformation of IPMCs was obtained under a water content of ∼70%. The peak value of the current and the water content at 3 Vpp driving voltage has also been observed.
